name: session-info
description: Session pane: context, cost and turns, the last turn's tokens, cache, tools and refused calls, a task list Claude keeps, an autopick switch that answers a question left unanswered with its recommended option, the skills in use, GitHub Actions runs, mentioned Jira issues, live plan usage bars, running agents with their model and effort, the shell commands Claude runs in the background, the last build and test run, background runs included, with a prompt that asks Claude to fix a failure and a switch that skips a build or test run when nothing changed since the same command passed, the Git state of the repository and its submodules with a treeview of its changed files, and a treeview of the files this session created, modified or deleted.

openOnStart.title: Open the pane when the session starts
openOnStart.description: Open the pane without /session-info. On a terminal narrower than 144 columns (110 after you opened the pane once), the pane waits until you widen the terminal or run /session-info.

showSession.title: Show the Session section
showSession.description: Context window as a stacked bar by category, cost, duration and turn stats.

showLastTurn.title: Show the Last turn section
showLastTurn.description: Result, duration and cost of the last turn, its model, effort and requests, token and cache counts, and the tools it called.

showTodos.title: Show the Todos section
showTodos.description: Give Claude a todo_write tool and show the task list it keeps for work with several steps. Off removes the tool and its prompt section.

todoMinSteps.title: Steps before a task list
todoMinSteps.description: The prompt section asks Claude to write a task list for work with at least this many distinct steps. 1 asks for a list for any work, but not for a question that needs only an answer.

todoInstruction.title: Task list instruction
todoInstruction.description: Your own text for the prompt section that tells Claude when to keep the task list, in place of the built-in one. Leave empty to use the built-in text with the step count above.

showAutopick.title: Show the Autopick section
showAutopick.description: A switch that answers a question Claude asked and you left unanswered with the option Claude marked (Recommended), after a wait you set in the section, with a countdown, Pick now and Cancel. The switch starts off. Off here hides the section and the /autopick command, and no question is answered for you.

showSkills.title: Show the Skills section
showSkills.description: The skills the conversation loaded and the agent that loaded each one. A skill stays active until the turn of its agent ends.

showCi.title: Show the CI section
showCi.description: Follow the GitHub Actions runs that a git push, gh pr create, gh workflow run or gh run rerun of the session started, with their jobs, a link and a notification at the end. Needs the GitHub CLI (gh), logged in.

showJira.title: Show the Jira section
showJira.description: Show the Jira issues the chat mentions, read through the connected Atlassian MCP server. The section stays hidden while no such server is connected.

jiraKeyPattern.title: Jira issue key pattern
jiraKeyPattern.description: A regular expression for your issue keys, for example WIN-\d+|ABC-\d+. Leave empty to show only the issues of /browse/ links and the issues Claude reads.

jiraSite.title: Jira site
jiraSite.description: Your Jira site URL, for example https://company.atlassian.net, or its cloud id. Leave empty to use the first Jira site the Atlassian account reaches.

showAgents.title: Show the Agents section
showAgents.description: Subagents and teammates of the session with their status, model and effort.

showBackground.title: Show the Background section
showBackground.description: The shell commands Claude started in the background, with their status and run time. A command shows as running until its task notification reaches the session.

showChecks.title: Show the Checks section
showChecks.description: Status of the last build and the last test run the session started, with error lines or failed test names, and the build guard switch, which skips a build or test run when nothing changed since the same command passed. Off also turns the build guard off.

suggestFix.title: Suggest a fix after a failed check
suggestFix.description: After a turn that leaves a failed build or test run, propose a prompt that asks Claude to fix it, such as Fix the 2 failed tests: A, B. Tab takes it. The proposal replaces the suggestion Claude Code makes after the turn, until the next prompt.

showGit.title: Show the Git section
showGit.description: Branch and upstream state, working-tree counts, the last commit, an operation in progress, the submodules that changed and a treeview of the changed files.

gitClient.title: Git client
gitClient.description: Command that the branch name (or g) opens in a new terminal window, in the repository root, for example lazygit, gitui or tig. Use double quotes around a path with spaces. Leave empty to turn it off.

showChanges.title: Show the Changes section
showChanges.description: Treeview of the files the session created, modified or deleted.

tabGroups.title: Tab groups
tabGroups.description: Sections that share one card as tabs. Separate groups with commas and the sections of a group with +, for example changes+git, ci+jira+skills. Names: session, lastTurn, todos, autopick, skills, ci, jira, usage, agents, background, checks, git, changes. The first section of a group is the tab it opens on. Leave empty to show each section in its own card.

sectionOrder.title: Section order
sectionOrder.description: The order of the sections, top to bottom, separated by commas, for example changes, git, session. Names: session, lastTurn, todos, autopick, skills, ci, jira, usage, agents, background, checks, git, changes. The sections you do not name follow in the default order. A tab group card sits where its first shown section sits in this order; the order of its tabs stays as Tab groups lists them. Leave empty for the default order.
sectionOrder.default: session, lastTurn, todos, autopick, skills, ci, jira, usage, agents, background, checks, git, changes

alerts.title: Usage and context alerts
alerts.description: Notify once when a usage window reaches 80% and 90%, and when the context window reaches 85%.

viewer.title: Diff viewer
viewer.description: auto: git diff.guitool, then VS Code, then inline. git: git difftool --gui. vscode: code --diff. inline: inside the pane.

editor.title: Editor for new files
editor.description: auto: VS Code when on the PATH, else the app the system associates with the file. vscode: code <file>. system: the associated app.

paneBackground.title: Pane background in the terminal
paneBackground.description: A color for the body of the pane in the terminal, as hex (#2e3440) or a color name, for example your terminal's background. Leave empty to keep the color Claude Code draws. The desktop app ignores it.

paneTitle.title: Pane title
paneTitle.description: A name for this pane, for example Personal or Work, to tell accounts apart. It is the pane's tab title and a one-row rule at the top of the pane. Leave empty for the default title, with no rule.

paneTitleColor.title: Pane title color
paneTitleColor.description: A color for the title rule at the top of the pane: hex (#ff8700), a color name or a theme key such as success or warning. It needs a pane title. Leave empty for the default text color.

paneTitleAlign.title: Pane title alignment
paneTitleAlign.description: Where the title sits on its rule: left, center or right. It needs a pane title.

icons.title: Icon set
icons.description: unicode works everywhere; nerd needs a Nerd Font; emoji needs a terminal that draws emoji two cells wide.

buildPattern.title: Extra build commands
buildPattern.description: A regular expression (case-insensitive) for more commands to treat as a build, matched against each command segment, for example ^make( |$). Leave empty for the built-in list.

testPattern.title: Extra test commands
testPattern.description: A regular expression (case-insensitive) for more commands to treat as a test run, for example ^just test|^task test. Leave empty for the built-in list.
